We have related from Abū Hurayra (may God be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The son of Mary is about to descend among you as a just judge: he will break the cross, kill the swine and abolish the poll-tax, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it; in his time all the religious communities will perish except Islam; and he will kill the Dajjāl, then remain on the earth forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him." Abū Hurayra said: Recite if you wish: And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death—before the death of Jesus son of Mary. Then Abū Hurayra would repeat it three times.

It is related from ʿIkrima that the pronoun in His words will surely believe in him refers to Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him); he says: no person of the People of the Book dies until he believes in Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

And it was said: it refers back to God, Mighty and Majestic; He says: there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in God, Mighty and Majestic, before his death, at the moment of seeing with his own eyes, when his faith will not benefit him.

His words, Exalted: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be, meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), a witness against them, that he conveyed to them the message of his Lord and acknowledged servanthood for himself, as He, Exalted, said, informing of him: and I was a witness over them as long as I was among them (5:117). Every prophet is a witness over his community; God, Exalted, said: So how will it be when We bring from every community a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these? (4:41).

His words, Exalted: When God said, "O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you" (5:110). Al-Ḥasan said: remembering the favour is giving thanks for it. By His words My favour He meant "My favours"; al-Ḥasan said: its wording is singular and its meaning plural, as in His words, Exalted: And if you were to count the favour of God, you could not number it (14:34; 16:18). "And upon your mother," Mary. Then He enumerated the favours and said: "When I strengthened you," fortified you, "with the Holy Spirit," meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him); "you spoke to people," meaning "and you spoke to people", "in the cradle," as an infant, "and in maturity," as a prophet. Ibn ʿAbbās said: He sent him when he was thirty years old, and he remained in his mission thirty months, then God raised him up to Himself. "And when I taught you the Book," meaning script, "and wisdom," meaning knowledge and understanding, "and the Torah and the Gospel; and when you created," made and formed, "from clay the likeness of a bird," like the form of a bird, "by My leave, then you breathed into it and it became a bird," alive and flying, "by My leave; and you healed," and made whole, "the one born blind and the leper by My leave; and when you brought forth the dead," from their graves, alive, "by My leave; and when I restrained," held back and turned away, "the Children of Israel," meaning the Jews, "from you," when they resolved to kill you, "when you came to them with the clear proofs," meaning the evidences and miracles, which are those we have mentioned.

"And those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is nothing but plain sorcery'," meaning the clear proofs he brought them. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read "a plain sorcerer" (sāḥir) here and in Sūrat Hūd and al-Ṣaff, so that it refers to Jesus (peace be upon him), and in Hūd it refers to Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him).

And when I inspired the disciples (5:111): I put it into their hearts and cast it into their breasts. Abū ʿUbayda said: meaning "I commanded", and ilā ("to") is a connective particle. The disciples are the select companions of Jesus (peace be upon him). "Believe in Me and in My messenger," Jesus. They said, when I granted them success, "We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims."
### When the disciples said, "O Jesus son of Mary, can your Lord…" (5:112)

Al-Kisāʾī read "can you" (hal tastaṭīʿu) with the tāʾ, and "your Lord" (rabbaka) with fatḥa on the bāʾ; this is the reading of ʿAlī, ʿĀʾisha, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid, that is: can you pray to and ask your Lord? The others read "can He" (hal yastaṭīʿu) with the yāʾ and "your Lord" (rabbuka) with ḍamma on the bāʾ. They did not say it as doubters of the power of God, Mighty and Majestic; rather its meaning is: will your Lord send it down or not? Just as a man says to his companion "can you get up and come with me?" when he knows that he can, and only means "will you do that or not?". And it was said: yastaṭīʿu has the sense of yuṭīʿu (to comply); one says aṭāʿa and istaṭāʿa with one meaning, as in their saying ajāba and istajāba; its meaning is: will your Lord comply with you by answering your request? And in the transmitted reports: "Whoever obeys God, God complies with him." Some took it according to the apparent sense and said: the people erred, and said it before their knowledge was firmly established, for they were human beings; so Jesus (peace be upon him) said to them, at the error, regarding their words as a grave matter, "Fear God, if you are believers", that is, do not doubt His power.

"to send down to us a table from heaven?" The table (māʾida) is the tray on which food is set. It is the active participle from mādahu, yamīduhu, "he gave to him and fed him", like their saying mārahu, yamīruhu (he provisioned him); and imtāda is the iftaʿala form from it. The māʾida is that which feeds food to those who eat; the food itself is also called a māʾida by extension, because it is eaten on the table. The people of Kūfa said: it was named māʾida because it sways (tamīdu) with those who eat, that is, it inclines. The people of Baṣra said: it is an active participle in the sense of the passive, that is, those who eat are drawn towards it, as in His words, Exalted, a pleasing life (ʿīshatin rāḍiya, 69:21; 101:7), that is, a life that is pleased with (marḍiyya). He said, that is Jesus (peace be upon him), answering them: "Fear God, if you are believers", so do not doubt His power. And it was said: fear God lest you ask of Him something that the communities before you did not ask of Him; so he forbade them from demanding signs after having believed.

That is: we ask only because we wish to eat of it (5:113), an eating for blessing, not an eating out of need, so that we may be certain of His power; and that our hearts may be at rest and stilled, and that we may know that you have told us the truth, that you are the Messenger of God; that is, that we may increase in faith and certainty. It was also said that Jesus son of Mary had commanded them to fast for thirty days, and that when they broke their fast they would ask nothing of God but that He would give it to them; so they did this and asked for the table, and said: "and that we may know that you have told us the truth" in what you said, that if we fasted thirty days we would ask nothing of God, Exalted, but that He would give it to us. And that we may be among the witnesses to it: witnesses for God to His oneness and His power, and for you to your prophethood and your mission. And it was said: and that we may be among those who bear witness for you before the Children of Israel when we return to them.

Jesus son of Mary said at that: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven (5:114). It was said that he performed a full ablution, put on haircloth, prayed two cycles of prayer, bowed his head, lowered his gaze and wept, and then said: O God, our Lord, send down to us a table from heaven, that it may be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us; that is, a return of favour (ʿāʾidah) from God upon us, a proof and a demonstration. The festival (ʿīd) is the day of rejoicing; it is so called because of the return (ʿawd) from grief to joy, and it is a name for whatever you have grown accustomed to and which returns to you. The day of Fast-breaking and the day of Sacrifice are called festival because they return every year. Al-Suddī said: Its meaning is: we shall take the day on which it was sent down as a festival for the first of us and the last of us; that is, we shall honour it, we and those who come after us. Sufyān said: We shall pray on it. His words for the first of us, that is, for the people of our own time, and the last of us, that is, for those who come after us. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The last of the people shall eat of it as the first of them ate. And a sign from You: an indication and a proof; and provide for us, and You are the best of providers.

God said, Exalted, answering Jesus (peace be upon him): I am sending it down to you (5:115), meaning the table. The people of Medina, Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read munazziluhā with doubling, because it came down several times, and the tafʿīl form indicates repetition, time after time; the others read it without doubling, in keeping with His words: send down to us. But whoever of you disbelieves after that, that is, after the sending down of the table, I shall punish him with a punishment, that is, a kind of punishment, with which I do not punish anyone among the worlds, meaning the people of his own age. The people then denied and disbelieved after the sending down of the table, and they were transformed into apes and swine. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: The people most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are the hypocrites, those who disbelieved among the people of the table, and the house of Pharaoh.

The scholars differed as to whether the table came down or not. Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan said: It did not come down, because when God, Mighty and Majestic, threatened them for disbelieving after the sending down of the table, they feared that some of them would disbelieve and so asked to be excused, saying: We do not want it; and so it did not come down. His words I am sending it down to you mean: if you ask.

The correct view, which is that of the majority, is that it did come down, because of His words, Exalted: I am sending it down to you, and there is no breach in His report, and because the reports about it from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), the Companions and the Followers are transmitted in unbroken abundance.

They differed as to its description. Khilās ibn ʿAmr related from ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), that it came down as bread and meat, and they were told: It will remain with you so long as you do not act treacherously or hoard; but their day had not passed before they acted treacherously and hoarded, and they were transformed into apes and swine.

Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: Jesus (peace be upon him) said to them: Fast thirty days, then ask of God what you will and He will give it to you. So they fasted, and when they had finished they said: O Jesus, had we worked for anyone and completed his work, he would have fed us. And they asked God for the table. Then the angels came forward bearing a table on which were seven loaves and seven fish, until they set it down before them, and the last of the people ate of it as the first of them had eaten.
Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: A table came down upside down, borne in flight by the angels between heaven and earth, and on it was every kind of food except meat.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās: There was sent down upon the table everything except bread and meat. Qatādah said: On it was fruit from the fruits of Paradise.
ʿAṭiyyah al-ʿAwfī said: There came down from heaven a fish in which was the taste of everything.
Al-Kalbī said: On it were bread, rice and green herbs.
Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God sent down loaves of barley and fish, and a group would eat and then go out, and others would come and eat, until all of them had eaten and there was some left over.

From al-Kalbī and Muqātil: God sent down bread and fish and five loaves, and they ate as much as God, Exalted, willed, the people being a thousand and some more. When they returned to their villages and spread the account, those who had not witnessed it laughed at them and said: Woe to you, he merely bewitched your eyes. Then whomever God wished well He kept firm in his insight, and whomever He wished to try returned to his unbelief; and they were transformed into swine, with no child or woman among them. They remained so for three days and then perished; they did not breed, nor eat, nor drink, and so it is with everyone who is transformed.

Qatādah said: It used to come down to them morning and evening wherever they were, like the manna and the quails for the Children of Israel. ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ related from Salmān al-Fārisī: When the disciples asked for the table, Jesus (peace be upon him) put on wool and wept, and said: "O God, send down to us a table from heaven," to the end of the verse. Then a red cloth came down between two clouds, a cloud above it and a cloud beneath it, while they looked at it as it swooped down, until it fell before them. Jesus wept and said: O God, make me one of the thankful; O God, make it a mercy and do not make it a punishment. The Jews looked upon a thing the like of which they had never seen, nor had they ever found a scent sweeter than its scent. Then Jesus (peace be upon him) said: Let the best of you in works rise, uncover it, and mention the name of God, Exalted. Simon the smith{{fn:Shamʿūn al-Ṣaffār, that is, Simon Peter, whom the commentators call the chief of the disciples.}}, the head of the disciples, said: You are more entitled to that than we are. So Jesus (peace be upon him) rose, performed the ablution, prayed a long prayer and wept much; then he uncovered the napkin from it and said: In the name of God, the best of providers. And there was a roasted fish without scales and without bones, dripping with fat, with salt at its head and vinegar at its tail, and around it all kinds of green herbs except leeks; and there were five loaves, on one of them olives, on the second honey, on the third clarified butter, on the fourth cheese, and on the fifth dried meat. Simon said: O Spirit of God, is this of the food of this world or of the food of the Hereafter? He said: Nothing of what you see is of the food of this world or of the food of the Hereafter; rather it is something that God, Exalted, has brought about by His overmastering power. Eat of what you asked for, and He will sustain you and increase you from His bounty. They said: O Spirit of God, be the first to eat of it. Jesus (peace be upon him) said: God forbid that I should eat of it; rather, let those who asked for it eat of it. But they were afraid to eat of it. So he summoned to it the needy, the sick, those afflicted with leprosy and elephantiasis, the crippled and the afflicted, and said: Eat of the provision of God; for you is the wholesome enjoyment, and for others the trial. So they ate, and a thousand and three hundred men and women, poor, sick, chronically ill and afflicted, rose from it, every one of them satisfied; and there was the fish in the very form it had when it came down. Then the cloth of the table flew upward while they looked at it, until it disappeared. No chronically ill person, no sick person and no afflicted person ate of it but was healed, and no poor person but was made rich; and those who had not eaten of it were filled with regret. It remained for forty mornings, coming down in the forenoon, and when it came down the rich and the poor, the young and the old, the men and the women would gather, and it would remain set out, eaten

from, until, when the shade turned, it flew away while they watched in its shadow until it disappeared from them. It came down on alternate days, coming down one day and not coming down the next, like the she-camel of Thamūd. Then God, Exalted, revealed to Jesus (peace be upon him): Make My table and My provision for the poor to the exclusion of the rich. This weighed heavily on the rich, until they doubted and made the people doubt concerning it, and said: Do you really think the table comes down from heaven? Then God, Exalted, revealed to Jesus (peace be upon him): I made it a condition that whoever disbelieved after it came down, I would punish him with a punishment with which I punish no one among the worlds. Jesus (peace be upon him) said: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118). Then three hundred and thirty men of them were transformed: they spent that night in their beds with their wives and in the morning were swine, running about in the roads and the rubbish heaps and eating excrement in the privies. When the people saw this they fled in alarm to Jesus (peace be upon him) and wept, and when the swine caught sight of Jesus (peace be upon him) they wept and began to circle around Jesus (peace be upon him), and Jesus began to call them by their names, and they would nod their heads and weep, unable to speak. They lived three days and then perished.

And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? He said: Glory be to You! It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your self; You are the Knower of the unseen things. (116) I said to them nothing but what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them so long as I remained among them; and when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. (117) If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise. (118)

His words, Mighty and Majestic: And when God said: O Jesus son of Mary, did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? (5:116). They differed as to when this saying takes place. Al-Suddī said: God, Exalted, said this to Jesus (peace be upon him) when He raised him to heaven, because the particle idh ("when") is used of the past. The rest of the commentators said: God will say this to him only on the Day of Resurrection, as shown by His words before it, on the day when God gathers the messengers (5:109), and His words after it, This is the day when the truthful shall profit by their truthfulness (5:119), by both of which He meant the Day of Resurrection. Idh may come with the meaning of idhā ("when" of the future), as in His words, Mighty and Majestic, If only you could see when they are terrified (34:51), that is, when they shall be terrified on the Day of Resurrection; and the Resurrection, though it has not yet come, is as though it had already come to pass, because it is coming without any doubt.

His words: Did you say to the people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides God? If it is asked: What is the point of this question, given God's knowledge, Mighty and Majestic, that Jesus did not say it?
It is answered: This question is put to him in order to rebuke his people and to magnify the gravity of this statement, just as one man says to another: Did you do such
and such? concerning something he knows he did not do, by way of informing him and expressing how grave it is, not by way of enquiry and seeking information.

Moreover, God, Mighty and Majestic, wished Jesus (peace be upon him) to confess of himself that he is a servant, so that his people should hear it and their lie against him, that he had commanded them to do that, should be exposed. Abū Rawq said: When Jesus (peace be upon him) hears this address, his joints will tremble and from the root of every hair on his body a spring of blood will burst forth; then he will say in answer to God, Mighty and Majestic: He said: Glory be to You!, declaring You far above that and magnifying You; It is not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Your self. Ibn ʿAbbās said: You know what is hidden in me, and I do not know what is hidden in You. It was said that its meaning is: You know my secret and I do not know Your secret. Abū Rawq said: You know what came from me in the abode of this world, and I do not know what will come from You in the Hereafter. Al-Zajjāj said: The "self" (nafs) is an expression for the whole of a thing and its reality; he is saying: You know all that I know of the reality of my affair, and I do not know the reality of Your affair. You are the Knower of the unseen things: what has been and what will be.

I said to them nothing but what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. And I was a witness over them so long as I remained among them; and when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things. (117)

I said to them nothing but what You commanded me: Worship God, my Lord and your Lord (5:117): declare Him one and associate nothing with Him; and I was a witness over them so long as I remained, that is, dwelt, among them; and when You took me up, took me and raised me to You, You were the Watcher over them, the Guardian over them, preserving their deeds, and You are Witness over all things.

His words, Exalted: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118). If it is asked: How did he seek forgiveness for them when they were unbelievers, and how did he say: and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise, when this is not fitting for a request for forgiveness? It is answered: As for the first, its meaning is: if You punish them for persisting in their unbelief, and if You forgive them after faith; and this holds good on the view of al-Suddī that this question takes place before the Day of Resurrection, because faith is of no avail on the Day of Resurrection.
It was also said: This concerns two groups among them, and its meaning is: if You punish those of them who disbelieved, and if You forgive those of them who believed.

It was also said: This is not by way of a request for forgiveness, for had it been so he would have said: You are the Forgiving, the Merciful; rather, it is by way of surrendering the matter and committing it to His will.

As for the second question: Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) used to read "and if You forgive them, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful", and so it stands in his codex. As for the well-known reading, it was said that there is a transposition in it, its sense being: if You forgive them, they are Your servants; and if You punish them, You are the Mighty, the Wise.

It was also said that its meaning is: if You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty in dominion, the Wise in judgement; nothing diminishes Your might, and nothing escapes Your judgement. The unbelievers come within the scope of His wisdom, His forgiveness and the vastness of His mercy and His forgiveness, but He has declared that He will not forgive, and He does not go back on what He has declared.

Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Qāhir informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Muḥammad al-Fārisī informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Julūdī related to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān related to us: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me: Ibn Wahb related to us: ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed me that Bakr ibn Sawādah related to him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited the words of God, Exalted, concerning Abraham: My Lord, they have led many of mankind astray; so whoever follows me is of me (14:36), to the end of the verse, and the words of Jesus (peace be upon him): If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise (5:118). Then he raised his hands and said: O God, my community! and wept. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: O Gabriel, go to Muḥammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes him weep. Gabriel came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) told him what he had said. Then God, Exalted, said: O Gabriel, go to Muḥammad and say: We shall satisfy you concerning your community, and We shall not grieve you.

God said: This is the day when the truthful shall profit by their truthfulness (5:119). Nāfiʿ read yawma with the mīm in the accusative, meaning: these things shall take place on a day; the "on" is omitted and so it takes the accusative. The others read it in the nominative, as the predicate of "this"; that is, the truthful in this world shall profit by their truthfulness in the Hereafter, whereas had they lied, God would have set a seal upon their mouths and their limbs would have spoken of it, and they would have been disgraced. It was also said that by "the truthful" the prophets are meant.

Al-Kalbī said: The believers shall profit by their faith. Qatādah said: Two speakers will not err on the Day of Resurrection: Jesus (peace be upon him), and that is what God, Mighty and Majestic, has related; and the enemy of God, Iblīs, and that is His words: And Satan said, when the matter had been decided (14:22), to the end of the verse. The enemy of God spoke the truth on that day, having been a liar before that, so his truthfulness did not profit him; whereas Jesus (peace be upon him) was truthful in this world and the Hereafter, so his truthfulness profited him.

ʿAṭāʾ said: This is a day among the days of this world, because the abode of the Hereafter is an abode of recompense, not an abode of works. Then He set out their reward, saying: Theirs are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein for ever; God is well pleased with them and they are well pleased with Him; that is the great triumph (5:119). Then He magnified Himself, saying: To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He has power over all things (5:120).
And dutiful to his parents (19:14), that is, devoted to them, gentle with them and good to them.

And he was not arrogant or disobedient. "The arrogant" (al-jabbār) is the proud; and it was said that "the arrogant" is one who strikes and kills in anger; and "the disobedient" (al-ʿaṣī) is the one who disobeys.

And peace be upon him (19:15), that is, safety be his, the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised up alive. Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah said: The most desolate that a man can be is in these three states: the day he is born, when he comes out of what he was in; the day he dies, when he sees people he had never beheld; and the day he is raised up, when he sees himself in a gathering the like of which he has never seen. So John was singled out for safety in these places.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: And mention in the Book, in the Qurʾān, Mary, when she withdrew, drew aside and secluded herself, from her people, from her kinsfolk, to an eastern place (19:16), that is, a place in the house on the side facing the east. It was a winter day of severe cold, and she sat in a sunny spot delousing her head.
It was also said: She had become clean from menstruation and went to wash herself.
Al-Ḥasan said: And it is from this that the Christians took the east as their direction of prayer.
And she took, set up, apart from them a screen (19:17). Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: a curtain.
It was also said: She sat behind a wall. Muqātil said: behind a mountain.

ʿIkrimah said: Mary used to stay in the sanctuary, and when she menstruated she would move to the house of her maternal aunt, and when she became clean she would return to the sanctuary. While she was washing herself after menstruation, having stripped herself, Gabriel appeared to her in the form of a beardless youth with a bright face, curly hair and a well-proportioned frame; and that is His words:

Then We sent to her Our Spirit, meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him), and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. It was also said that what is meant by the Spirit is Jesus (peace be upon him), who came in the form of a man and she conceived him; but the first is more correct. When Mary saw Gabriel making towards her, she called out to him from afar, and she said: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing (19:18), that is, a believer and obedient.
If it is asked: Refuge is sought only from the wicked, so how did she say: I seek refuge in the All-Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing?
It is answered: This is like someone saying: If you are a believer, do not wrong me; that is, your faith ought to restrain you from wrongdoing. So it is here.
Its meaning is: and your fear of God ought to restrain you from wickedness.

He said, Gabriel said to her: I am only a messenger of your Lord, that I may grant you (19:19). Nāfiʿ and the people of Basra read li-yahaba laki with yāʾ, that is, that your Lord may grant you; the others read li-ahaba laki, attributing the act to the messenger, although the gift is from God, Exalted, because he was sent with it.
A pure boy: a righteous child, pure from sins.

She said, Mary said: How, from where, shall I have a boy when no man has touched me, no husband has come near me, and I have not been unchaste? (19:20), a wanton woman. She means that a child comes either from marriage or from fornication, and neither of the two had taken place here.

He said, Gabriel said: So it shall be (19:21). It was said that its meaning is: it is as you say, O Mary, but your Lord has said; and it was said: thus has your Lord said: It is easy for Me, that is, the creation of a child without a father; and that We may make him a sign, a token, for mankind, and a proof of Our power, and a mercy from Us, and a blessing for whoever follows him in his religion; and it was, that, a matter decreed, decided and settled, which is neither turned back nor altered.
His words, Mighty and Majestic: So she conceived him (19:22). It was said that Gabriel lifted her shift and breathed into its opening, and she conceived when she put it on.
It was also said: He stretched out the opening of her shift with his finger and then breathed into the opening.
It was also said: He breathed into the sleeve of her garment. And it was said: into her mouth.

It was also said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) breathed a breath from afar, and the breath reached her and she conceived Jesus at once. And she withdrew with him, that is, she drew aside with the pregnancy and secluded herself, to a far place, far from her people.

Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: The farthest end of the valley, which is the valley of Bethlehem, fleeing from her people lest they reproach her for giving birth without a husband.
They differed as to the length of her pregnancy and the time of her delivery. Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: The conception and the birth took place in a single hour.
It was also said: The length of her pregnancy was nine months, like the pregnancy of other women.
It was also said: The length of her pregnancy was eight months, and that was another sign, because no child born at eight months survives, yet Jesus was born after this period and lived.
It was also said: She gave birth after six months.

Muqātil ibn Sulaymān said: Mary conceived him in an hour, he was formed in an hour, and she gave birth to him in an hour, when the sun declined on that same day, she being a girl of ten years, and she had menstruated twice before she conceived Jesus.

And it drove her, that is, it compelled her and brought her, the pangs of childbirth, which are the pain of labour, to the trunk of the palm tree (19:23). It was a dry palm tree in the desert, in the depth of winter, with no fronds on it.

It was also said: She took refuge at it in order to lean against it and hold on to it through the pain of childbirth. She said: Would that I had died before this: she wished for death out of shame before people and fear of disgrace; and had been a thing forgotten. Ḥamzah and Ḥafṣ read nasyan with fatḥah on the nūn, and the rest with kasrah; they are two dialectal forms, like al-watr and al-witr, and al-jisr and al-jasr. It means the thing forgotten, and al-nasy in the language is everything that is cast away, forgotten and not mentioned because of its insignificance.

Forgotten, that is, abandoned. Qatādah said: Something that is neither known nor mentioned. ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Mujāhid said: A carcass thrown away. And it was said: She means, had I never been created.

Then he called to her from beneath her (19:24). Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ read min taḥtihā with kasrah on the mīm and the tāʾ, meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him): Mary was on a hillock and Gabriel was behind the hillock, below her, and he called to her.

The others read it with fatḥah on the mīm and the tāʾ{{fn:That is, man taḥtahā, "he who was beneath her called to her".}}, and they too intended Gabriel (peace be upon him): he called to her from the foot of the mountain.
It was also said: It was Jesus who, when he came out of his mother's womb, called to her: Do not grieve. This is the view of Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan.

The first is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), al-Suddī, Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and a group: that the caller was Gabriel, who, when he heard her words and recognised her distress, called to her: Do not grieve.
Your Lord has placed beneath you a rivulet. "The rivulet" (al-sarī) is the small stream.
It was also said: "beneath you" means that God placed it under your command: if you order it to flow, it flows, and if you order it to hold back, it holds back.

Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: Gabriel (peace be upon him), or, as it is also said, Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), struck the earth with his foot, and a spring of sweet water appeared and flowed.
It was also said: There was a dry stream there, in which God, Glorified and Exalted, made the water flow, and the dry palm tree came to life, put forth leaves, bore fruit and ripened fresh dates.
Al-Ḥasan said: "beneath you a sarī" means Jesus, and by God he was a noble (sarī) servant, meaning exalted.

And shake towards you, that is, Mary was told: move, the trunk of the palm tree (19:25). The Arabs say hazzahu and hazza bihi, just as one says ḥazza raʾsahu and ḥazza bi-raʾsihi, and amdada al-ḥabla and amdada bihi. It will let fall upon you: the well-known reading is with fatḥah on the tāʾ and the qāf and doubling of the sīn, that is, tatasāqaṭu, one of the two tāʾs being assimilated into the sīn; that is, the palm tree will let fall upon you fresh dates. Ḥamzah read the sīn without doubling and dropped the tāʾ which the others assimilated.
Ḥafṣ read it with ḍammah on the tāʾ and kasrah on the qāf, without doubling, on the pattern of tufāʿilu; tusāqiṭu has the meaning of asqaṭa, and the feminine form is on account of the palm tree.
Yaʿqūb read yassāqaṭu with yāʾ and doubling, referring it back to the trunk.

Fresh ripe dates: gathered dates. It was also said that al-janī is that which has reached its full ripeness and whose time of gathering has come. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym said: In my view there is nothing better for the woman in childbed than fresh dates, nor anything better for the sick than honey. His words, Glorified and Exalted: So eat and drink (19:26), that is, eat, O Mary, of the fresh dates and drink of the water of the stream, and be comforted, literally "cool your eye", that is, be of good cheer. It was also said: Let your eye be cooled by your child Jesus. One says: May God cool your eye, meaning: may your heart meet with what pleases you, so that your eye rests from looking at anything else. It was also said: "God cooled his eye" means He put it to sleep; one says qarra yaqirru when a thing becomes still.
It was also said: When the eye weeps from joy the tears are cool, and when it weeps from grief the tears are hot; and from this it is said: May God cool his eye, and: May God heat his eye.
And if you see any human being, that is, taray, upon which the nūn of emphasis has entered, and the yāʾ takes kasrah because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters.

Its meaning is: if you see any human being who asks you about your child, say: I have vowed to the All-Merciful a fast, that is, a silence; and so Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) used to read it.
Fasting (ṣawm) in the language is abstention from food, drink and speech.
Al-Suddī said: Among the Children of Israel, whoever wished to exert himself in devotion would fast from speech as he fasted from food, and would not speak until evening.
It was also said that God, Exalted, commanded her to say this by a gesture.
It was also said that He commanded her to say this much aloud, and then to refrain from speech after it.
So I shall not speak today to any human being. It is said: She used to speak to the angels and not speak to human beings.
Then she brought him to her people, carrying him (19:27). It was said that she gave birth to him and then carried him at once to her people.

Al-Kalbī said: Joseph the carpenter carried Mary and her son Jesus (peace be upon them both) to a cave, and she remained forty days until she was clean from the bleeding of childbirth; then Mary (peace be upon her) carried him to her people, and Jesus (peace be upon him) spoke to her on the way, saying: O mother, rejoice, for I am the servant of God and His Messiah. When she came in to her family with the child, they wept and grieved, for they were a righteous household. They said: O Mary, you have done a monstrous thing: a grave and abominable thing. Abū ʿUbaydah said: Every extraordinary matter, whether a wonder or a deed, is farī.
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said of ʿUmar: "I have never seen a master who does his work as he does (yafrī fariyyahu)", that is, who performs his deed.

O sister of Aaron (19:28). He means: O you who resemble Aaron. Qatādah and others said: Aaron was a righteous and devout man among the Children of Israel. It is related that on the day he died, forty thousand men, every one of them named Aaron, from among the Children of Israel followed his funeral, besides the rest of the people. They likened her to him in the sense of: we thought you were like him in righteousness. Brotherhood by lineage is not meant by it, just as God, Exalted, said: The squanderers are the brothers of the devils (17:27), that is, their likes.

Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Qāhir informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Muḥammad informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā informed us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān informed us: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj related to us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to us: Ibn Idrīs related to us, from his father, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wāʾil, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, who said: When I came to Najrān they questioned me, saying: You recite O sister of Aaron, yet Moses was so-and-so long before Jesus! When I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) I asked him about that, and he said: "They used to name themselves after their prophets and the righteous who were before them."
Al-Kalbī said: Aaron was Mary's brother on her father's side, and he was the most exemplary man among the Children of Israel.
Al-Suddī said: They meant by it only Aaron the brother of Moses, because she was of his descent, just as one says to a man of Tamīm: O brother of Tamīm.
It was also said: Aaron was a wicked man among the Children of Israel, greatly given to wickedness, and they likened her to him.

Your father, ʿImrān, was not a man of evil. Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: a fornicator; nor was your mother, Ḥannah, unchaste, that is, a fornicatress; so from where have you got this child?
Then she pointed, Mary pointed, to him, that is, to Jesus (peace be upon him), meaning: speak to him (19:29).
Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) said: Since she had no argument, she pointed to him so that his speech might be her argument.
In the story it is related that when she pointed to him the people grew angry and said: On top of what you have done, do you mock us?
They said: How shall we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?, that is, one who is in the cradle, which was her lap.

It was also said: It is the cradle itself, and kāna ("was") has the meaning of "is". Abū ʿUbaydah said: kāna is redundant, that is: how shall we speak to a child in the cradle? Kāna may occur in speech as a filler with no meaning, as in His words Was I ever anything but a human being, a messenger? (17:93), that is: am I anything but?
Al-Suddī said: When Jesus heard their words he left off suckling and turned to face them.
It was also said: When she pointed to him, he left the breast, leaned on his left side, turned to face them, and began to gesture with his right hand:

He said: I am the servant of God (19:30). Wahb said: Zachariah came to her during her dispute with the Jews and said to Jesus: Speak your argument, if you have been commanded to. Then Jesus (peace be upon him) said, being forty days old, though Muqātil said: rather, it was on the day he was born: I am the servant of God. He confessed of himself servanthood to God, Mighty and Majestic, as the first thing he spoke, lest he be taken as a god. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet. It was said that its meaning is: He will give me the Book and make me a prophet.

It was also said: This is a report of what was written for him in the Preserved Tablet, just as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: When were you a prophet? and he said: "I was a prophet when Adam was between the spirit and the body."
The majority said: He was given the Gospel while he was a small child, and he had the understanding of grown men.
From al-Ḥasan it is related that he said: He was inspired with the Torah while he was in his mother's womb.

And He has made me blessed wherever I may be (19:31), that is, of great benefit wherever I turn. Mujāhid said: a teacher of good. ʿAṭāʾ said: calling to God, to His oneness and His worship. It was also said: blessed for whoever follows me.
And He has enjoined on me prayer and almsgiving, that is, He commanded me to perform them both.
If it is asked: Jesus had no wealth, so how could he be commanded to give alms?
It is answered: Its meaning is: almsgiving, had I wealth. It was also said: the doing of abundant good.

So long as I live. And dutiful to my mother (19:32), that is, and He has made me dutiful to my mother; and He has not made me arrogant or wretched, that is, disobedient to his Lord. It was said: "the wretched" (al-shaqī) is one who sins and does not repent.
And peace be upon me the day I was born (19:33), that is, safety at birth from the prodding of Satan.
And the day I die,

that is, at death, safety from associating partners with God; and the day I am raised up alive, safety from the terrors. When Jesus spoke to them with this, they knew Mary's innocence. Then Jesus (peace be upon him) fell silent and did not speak after that until he reached the age at which children speak.

That is Jesus son of Mary (19:34). Al-Zajjāj said: that is, the one who said "I am the servant of God" is Jesus son of Mary. The word of truth: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read qawla al-ḥaqqi with the lām in the accusative, which is the accusative of the verbal noun, that is: he spoke the word of truth; concerning which they are in doubt, that is, concerning which they differ: one says he is the son of God, another says he is God, and another says he is a lying sorcerer.

The others read it with the lām in the nominative, meaning: he is the word of truth, that is, this speech is the word of truth; the word is annexed to the truth, as He said "the truth of certainty" and "the promise of truth".

It was also said that it is an epithet of Jesus son of Mary, meaning: that is Jesus son of Mary, the word of God; "the Truth" is God, concerning whom they are in doubt, doubting and differing and saying what is not true. Then He denied of Himself the having of a child, saying: It is not for God to take any child (19:35), that is, taking a child is not among His attributes. It was also said: the lām is transposed, that is: God was not one to take any child. Glory be to Him! When He decrees a matter, when He wills to bring a matter into being, He only says to it: Be! and it is. And God is my Lord and your Lord (19:36): the people of the Ḥijāz and Abū ʿAmr read anna Allāha with fatḥah on the alif, referring back to His words and He has enjoined on me prayer and almsgiving and "that God is my Lord and your Lord"; the people of Syria and Kufa and Yaʿqūb read it with kasrah on the alif, as the beginning of a new sentence. So worship Him. This is a straight path. Then the factions differed among themselves (19:37), meaning the Christians; they were called factions because they split into three parties over the matter of Jesus: the Nestorians, the Melkites and the Jacobites.
So woe to those who disbelieve from the witnessing of a tremendous day, meaning the Day of Resurrection.

So We answered him and granted him John (21:90), as a son, and We set right for him his wife, that is, We made her able to bear children after she had been barren; so said most of the commentators. Some of them said: She was ill-tempered, and He set her right for him by granting her a good temper.

They, meaning the prophets whom He has named in this sūrah, used to hasten to good works and call upon Us in longing, in hope, and in dread, in fear: longing for the mercy of God and dread of the punishment of God; and they were humble before Us, that is, lowly. Qatādah said: submissive to the command of God. Mujāhid said: Humility is the abiding fear in the heart.

And she who guarded her chastity (21:91), kept it from what is forbidden; He means Mary daughter of ʿImrān. And We breathed into her of Our Spirit, that is, We commanded Gabriel until he breathed into the opening of her shift, and by that breath We brought the Messiah into being in her womb; and He attributed the Spirit to Himself as an honour to Jesus (peace be upon him). And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds, that is, a proof of the perfection of Our power to create a child without a father. He did not say "two signs", though they are two signs, because the meaning of the words is: We made their condition and their affair a sign; and because the sign in the two of them was one, namely that she brought him forth without a male.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: This your community (21:92), that is, your religious community and your religion, is one community, that is, one religion, which is Islam; so He declared void every religion other than Islam. The root sense of "community" (ummah) is the group that is bent on a single aim, so the revealed law was made "one community" because its people are united upon a single aim. "Community" takes the accusative as a detached qualifier.
And I am your Lord, so worship Me.

But they split up their affair among themselves; all shall return to Us. (93) So whoever does righteous deeds while a believer, there shall be no denial of his endeavour, and We are recording it for him. (94) And it is forbidden for any town We have destroyed that they shall not return, (95) until, when Gog and Magog are let loose and they come swarming down from every height. (96)

But they split up their affair among themselves (21:93), that is, they differed in religion and became sects and factions. Al-Kalbī said: They divided their religion among themselves, cursing one another and disowning one another. "Splitting up" (taqaṭṭuʿ) here has the sense of "cutting up" (taqṭīʿ). All shall return to Us, and We shall recompense them for their deeds.

So whoever does righteous deeds while a believer, there shall be no denial of his endeavour (21:94): his endeavour shall not be denied nor made void; rather, it shall be acknowledged with thanks and rewarded. And We are recording it for him: preserving his deed. It was also said: The meaning of "thanks" on the part of God is recompense.

And it is forbidden for any town (21:95). Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr read wa-ḥirmun with kasrah on the ḥāʾ and without alif, while the rest read it with alif, ḥarāmun; they are two dialectal forms, like ḥill and ḥalāl.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: The meaning of the verse is: and it is forbidden for any town, that is, the people of any town, We have destroyed, that they should return after destruction; on this view the "not" is redundant. Others said: "forbidden" has the meaning of "incumbent", and on this view the "not" stands in its own meaning; its sense is: it is incumbent upon the people of any town We have destroyed that they shall not return to this world.

Al-Zajjāj said: Its meaning is: and it is forbidden for the people of any town We have destroyed, that is, whose destruction We have decreed, that their deeds should be accepted, because they do not return, that is, they do not repent. The proof of this meaning is that He said in the verse before it: So whoever does righteous deeds while a believer, there shall be no denial of his endeavour, that is, his deed is accepted, and then mentioned this verse immediately after it and made plain that the unbeliever's deed is not accepted.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: Until, when they are let loose (21:96). Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb read futtiḥat with doubling, to express abundance, and the others read it without doubling. Gog and Magog: He means that the barrier is opened to release Gog and Magog, and they from every height, that is, every rise and hill, the ḥadab being the elevated place, come swarming down, hastening down from the hillocks and hills like the loping of the wolf, which is the swiftness of its gait. They differed about this pronoun. One group said: Gog and Magog are meant by it, as shown by what we have related from al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān, from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: "And God will send Gog and Magog, and they will come swarming down from every height." Another group said: He meant all created beings, that is, that they come out of their graves; this is supported by the reading of Mujāhid, "and they from every grave (jadath)", with jīm and thāʾ, as He said: And behold, from the graves to their Lord they come swarming (36:51).

Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Muḥammad al-Fārisī informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Julūdī informed us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān informed us: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj informed us: Abū Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb informed us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Furāt al-Qazzāz, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Usayd al-Ghifārī, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) looked in on us while we were talking among ourselves, and said: What are you discussing? They said: We are discussing the Hour. He said: "It will not come until you see ten signs before it," and he mentioned the smoke, the Antichrist, the beast, the rising of the sun from its place of setting, the descent of Jesus son of Mary, Gog and Magog, and three sinkings of the earth: a sinking in the west, a sinking in the east and a sinking in the Arabian peninsula; "and the last of these is a fire that will come out of Yemen, driving the people to their place of gathering."
Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a manifest authority (23:45), that is, with a clear proof: the hand, the staff and others besides.
To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were arrogant (23:46), they held themselves too great for faith, and they were a haughty people: proud, subduing others by oppression.

And they said (23:47), meaning Pharaoh and his people: Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves, meaning Moses and Aaron, while their people are our servants?, obedient to us and abased before us; the Arabs call everyone who submits to a king his "servant" (ʿābid).
So they denied them both and were among those destroyed (23:48), by drowning.
And We gave Moses the Book (23:49), the Torah, that they might be guided, that is, so that his people might be guided by it.

And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign (23:50), a proof of Our power. He did not say "two signs". It was said that its meaning is: their condition is a sign. It was also said that its meaning is: We made each one of them a sign, as in His words, Exalted: Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce (18:33).

And We gave them refuge on a height. The height (rabwah) is the elevated piece of ground. Opinions about it differed. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām said: It is Damascus, and this is the view of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and Muqātil. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The Ghūṭah of Damascus. Abū Hurayrah said: It is Ramla. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbās: It is Jerusalem, and this is the view of Qatādah and Kaʿb. Kaʿb said: It is the nearest part of the earth to heaven, by eighteen miles. Ibn Zayd said: It is Egypt. Al-Suddī said: The land of Palestine.
Possessing a place of rest, that is, level, spread out and spacious, upon which those who dwell there may settle.
And a flowing spring. The maʿīn is the running water, visible to the eye, which the eyes see; it is a passive participle from ʿānahu yaʿīnuhu, when sight perceives a thing.
So when they had angered Us (43:55), provoked Us to wrath, We took vengeance on them and drowned them all together.

And We made them a precedent (43:56). Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read sulufan with ḍammah on the sīn and the lām. Al-Farrāʾ said: It is the plural of salīf, from salufa, with ḍammah on the lām, yaslufu, that is, to go before. The others read it with fatḥah on the sīn and the lām, as the plural of sālif, like ḥāris and ḥaras, khādim and khadam, and rāṣid and raṣad. Both mean those of the nations who have passed away and gone before. One says salufa yaslufu when someone goes before, and the salaf are those of the forefathers who went before. So We made them go before, that others might take warning from them.

And an example for those who come after: a lesson and an admonition for those who remained after them. It was also said: a precedent to the Fire for the unbelievers of this community, and an example for those who come after them.

And when the son of Mary is cited as an example (43:57). Ibn ʿAbbās and most of the commentators said: The verse was revealed concerning the dispute of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about Jesus (peace be upon him), when His words, Mighty and Majestic, You and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell (21:98) were revealed; and we have recounted it in the sūrah of the Prophets (peace be upon them). Behold, your people cry out at it. The people of Medina and Syria and al-Kisāʾī read yaṣuddūna with ḍammah on the ṣād, that is, they turn away; its parallel is His words, Exalted, turning away from you in aversion (4:61). The others read it with kasrah on the ṣād.
They differed about its meaning. Al-Kisāʾī said: They are two dialectal forms, like yaʿrushūna and yaʿrishūna, shadda ʿalayhi yashuddu and yashiddu, and namma bi-l-ḥadīthi yanummu and yanimmu.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: Its meaning is: they clamour. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: they shout. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they cry aloud. Qatādah said: they are dismayed. Al-Quraẓī said: they are vexed. "And when the son of Mary is cited as an example, behold, your people cry out at it", saying: Muḥammad wants nothing from us but that we should worship him and take him as a god, as the Christians worshipped Jesus.
And they say: Are our gods better, or he? (43:58). Qatādah said: By "or he" they mean Muḥammad; so that we should worship him and obey him and abandon our gods.

Al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd said: "or he" means Jesus. They said: Muḥammad claims that everything worshipped besides God is in the Fire; well, we are content for our gods to be with Jesus, Ezra and the angels in the Fire. God, Exalted, said: They cite it, meaning this example, to you only for the sake of argument, disputation by falsehood; for they knew that what is meant by His words "and what you worship besides God are the fuel of Hell" (21:98) is these idols.
Rather, they are a contentious people.

Abū Saʿīd al-Shurayḥī informed us: Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī informed us: Abū Bakr ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥamshāwī informed us: Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥamdān al-Qaṭīʿī informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal related to us: my father related to me: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr related to us: Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār al-Wāsiṭī related to us, from Abū Ghālib, from Abū Umāmah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No people have gone astray after guidance they were upon except that they were given to argument," and then he recited: They cite it to you only for the sake of argument; rather, they are a contentious people (43:58).

Then He mentioned Jesus, saying: He is not (43:59), he is nothing, meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), but a servant on whom We bestowed favour, by prophethood, and We made him an example, a sign and a lesson, for the Children of Israel, by which they might know the power of God, Mighty and Majestic, over whatever He wills, in that He created him without a father.

And had We willed, We could have made from among you angels (43:60), that is, had We willed, We would have destroyed you and put angels in your place, to succeed in the earth, to be successors to you, populating the earth and worshipping Me and obeying Me. It was also said: succeeding one another.

And he (43:61), meaning Jesus (peace be upon him), is indeed a means of knowledge of the Hour, meaning that his descent is one of the portents of the Hour, by which its nearness is known. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayrah and Qatādah read "and he is indeed a mark (ʿalam) of the Hour", with fatḥah on the lām and the ʿayn, that is, a token and a sign.

We have related from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "The son of Mary is surely about to descend among you as a just judge; he will break the cross, kill the swine and abolish the poll-tax, and in his time all religious communities will perish except Islam."

It is related: "He will descend upon a mountain pass in the Holy Land, wearing two garments dyed pale yellow, with the hair of his head oiled and a spear in his hand, which is the one with which he will kill the Antichrist. He will come to Jerusalem while the people are at the afternoon prayer, and the imam will step back, but Jesus will put him forward and pray behind him according to the law of Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Then he will kill the swine, break the cross, demolish the synagogues and churches, and kill the Christians except those who believe in him."

ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Malīḥī informed us: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī informed us: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf informed us: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl related to us: Ibn Bukayr related to us: al-Layth related to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from Nāfiʿ the client of Abū Qatādah al-Anṣārī, that Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "How will you be when the son of Mary descends among you and your imam is from among you?"

Al-Ḥasan and a group said: "And it", meaning: and the Qurʾān is indeed a means of knowledge of the Hour; it teaches you of its coming and informs you of its conditions and its terrors. So do not doubt concerning it, have no doubt about it. Ibn ʿAbbās said: do not deny it. And follow me, upon the affirmation of God's oneness; this, which I am upon, is a straight path.
And let not (43:62), let him not turn you away, Satan, from the religion of God; he is indeed a manifest enemy to you.

And when Jesus came with the clear proofs, he said: I have come to you with wisdom (43:63), with prophethood, and to make plain to you some of that over which you differ, of the rulings of the Torah. Qatādah said: He means the differing of the parties who split into factions over the matter of Jesus. Al-Zajjāj said: What Jesus brought in the Gospel is only some of that over which they differed, and he made plain to them outside the Gospel what they needed.
So fear God and obey me.

God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path. (64) Then the factions differed among themselves; so woe to those who do wrong from the punishment of a painful day. (65) Are they waiting for anything but the Hour (43:66), meaning that it will come to them without fail, so it is as though they are waiting for it, that it should come upon them suddenly, unexpectedly, while they do not perceive?

And We sent Noah and Abraham, and We placed prophethood and the Book among their descendants; and among them are some who are guided, but many of them are rebellious. (26) Then We sent in their footsteps Our messengers, and We sent after them Jesus son of Mary and gave him the Gospel, and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him (57:27), in his religion, compassion, which is the most intense tenderness, and mercy: they were affectionate towards one another, as God, Exalted, said in describing the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), merciful among themselves (48:29). And monasticism which they innovated, of their own accord. This is not in apposition to what precedes it; it takes the accusative by an implied verb, as though He said: and they innovated monasticism, that is, they brought it of their own accord. We did not prescribe it, that is, We did not make it obligatory, for them, only seeking the good pleasure of God, meaning: but they sought the good pleasure of God by that monasticism. That monasticism was the hardships they imposed upon themselves in abstaining from food, drink, clothing and marriage, and in devoting themselves to worship in the mountains. But they did not observe it with its due observance, that is, they did not observe monasticism with its due observance; rather, they neglected it, disbelieved in the religion of Jesus, became Jews and Christians, entered into the religion of their kings and abandoned the monastic life. Some of them remained upon the religion of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) until they met Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and believed in him, and that is His words, Exalted: So We gave those of them who believed their reward, and they are those who remained steadfast in it, the people of compassion and mercy; but many of them are rebellious, and they are those who abandoned monasticism and disbelieved in the religion of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him).

Abū Saʿīd al-Shurayḥī informed us: Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī informed us: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥāmid informed me: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī informed us: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān related to us: Shaybān ibn Farrūkh related to us: al-Ṣaʿq ibn Ḥazn related to us, from ʿAqīl al-Jaʿdī, from Abū Isḥāq, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, from Ibn Masʿūd (may God, Exalted, be pleased with him), who said: I went in to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and he said: "O Ibn Masʿūd, those before you split into seventy-two sects, of which three were saved and the rest perished. One sect stood up against the kings and fought them for the religion of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him), and they seized them and killed them. Another sect had no strength to stand against the kings, nor to remain among them calling them to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus (peace be upon him), so they wandered through the lands and took up the monastic life, and they are those of whom God, Mighty and Majestic, said: And monasticism which they innovated; We did not prescribe it for them." Then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever believes in me, affirms me and follows me has observed it with its due observance, and whoever does not believe in me, those are the ones who perish."

It is related from Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) that he said: I was riding behind the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) on a donkey, and he said to me: "O Ibn Umm ʿAbd, do you know from where the Children of Israel took monasticism?" I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: "Tyrants prevailed over them after Jesus (peace be upon him), committing acts of disobedience, and the people of faith were angered and fought them, and the people of faith were defeated three times, until only a few of them remained. They said: If we show ourselves to these people they will annihilate us, and no one will remain to call to the religion. So they said: Come, let us scatter through the earth until God sends the prophet whom Jesus (peace be upon him) promised us," meaning Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). "So they scattered into the caves of the mountains and instituted monasticism; some of them held fast to their religion and some of them disbelieved." Then he recited this verse: And monasticism which they innovated, to the end of the verse. So We gave those of them who believed, meaning those who remained steadfast in it, their reward. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O Ibn Umm ʿAbd, do you know what the monasticism of my community is?" I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: "Emigration, striving in God's cause, prayer, fasting, the pilgrimage, the lesser pilgrimage, and proclaiming God's greatness upon the hills."
It is related from Anas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: "Every community has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this community is striving in the cause of God."

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) that he said: After Jesus (peace be upon him) there were kings who altered the Torah and the Gospel, and among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel and called them to the religion of God. It was said to their kings: If only you would gather these people who are making trouble for you, and either kill them or have them enter into what we are in. So their kings gathered them and offered them death, or else that they abandon the reading of the Torah and the Gospel except what they had altered of them. They said: We will spare you the trouble of dealing with us. One party said: Build us a pillar, then raise us up onto it, then give us something by which we can draw up our food and drink, and we shall not come back to you. Another party said: Leave us to wander through the earth and roam, and drink as the wild beasts drink; and if you find us in any land, kill us. Another party said: Build us dwellings in the wildernesses; we shall dig wells and cultivate herbs, and we shall not come back to you nor pass by you. So they did this for them, and those people went on in the way of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him). After them there came a generation of those who had altered the Book, and a man would say: We shall be in the place of so-and-so and worship as so-and-so worshipped, and wander as so-and-so wandered, and take dwellings as so-and-so took dwellings; yet they were in their polytheism, with no knowledge of the faith of those whom they imitated. That is His words, Mighty and Majestic: "And monasticism which they innovated", that is, these righteous people innovated it; but they did not observe it with its due observance, meaning the later ones who came after them; so We gave those of them who believed their reward, meaning those who innovated it seeking the good pleasure of God; "but many of them are rebellious", and they are those who came after them. He said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent, and only a few of them remained, a man came down from his hermitage, a wanderer came from his wandering, and the keeper of a monastery came from his monastery, and they believed in him.
Then God, Mighty and Majestic, said: O you who believe, fear God (57:28).

And when Jesus son of Mary said: O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what is before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger who will come after me, whose name is Aḥmad (61:6). The alif in it is for intensification in praise (ḥamd), and it has two aspects. The first is that it is an intensive form of the agent: that is, all the prophets are great praisers of God, Mighty and Majestic, and he praises God more than any other. The second is that it is an intensive form of the object: that is, all the prophets are praised for the praiseworthy qualities in them, and he is the most intensely praised of them and the most comprehensive in the virtues and excellences for which one is praised.
But when he came to them with the clear proofs, they said: This is manifest sorcery.

And who does greater wrong than one who forges a lie against God while he is being called to Islam? And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. (7) They wish to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light, though the unbelievers hate it. (8)
It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists hate it. (9)

O you who believe, shall I direct you to a trade that will save you (61:10). Ibn ʿĀmir read tunajjīkum with doubling, and the others without doubling. From a painful punishment. This was revealed when they said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, Mighty and Majestic, we would do them. He made that the equivalent of a trade, because by it they gain the good pleasure of God, the attainment of His Paradise and salvation from the Fire. Then He set out that trade, saying:

You shall believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives; that is better for you, if you only knew. (11) He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, and goodly dwellings in the gardens of Eden; that is the great triumph. (12)
